top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct, mature and independently reproduced measurement advance: the magic-wavelength trapping idea (Katori) and its realisation and precision development (Ye) give interrogation of many atoms free of Doppler, recoil and light-shift perturbation, with uncertainties near 1e-18 confirmed by several laboratories. It is separate from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, the Katori and Ye allocation is clean, and the citation scope is accurate. No award is not preferable when a ripe, well-verified candidate is available.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Lund atomic-physics and laser-spectroscopy background overlaps in field, but no specific connection to Katori or Ye is evident
